edits.note: Q3: mechanism class in the differential

edits.html:
Bleeding by mechanism Normal PT (prothrombin time) and aPTT (activated partial thromboplastin time) argue against a clotting factor deficiency and against DIC (disseminated intravascular coagulation). A low platelet count with a normal hemoglobin and white count in a well child means increased platelet destruction. In ITP (immune thrombocytopenia), antibodies coat platelets and splenic macrophages clear them; the antibodies also reduce platelet production. Decreased production from leukemia or aplastic anemia usually lowers two or more cell lines. Abnormal platelet function (von Willebrand disease, Glanzmann thrombasthenia) causes bleeding at a normal or near-normal count.
How NBME framed it The key was a mechanism class, increased platelet destruction, not the name ITP (immune thrombocytopenia). Child abuse was the decoy, planted as an active boy with bruises in several stages of healing. Widespread petechiae, a platelet count of 1,000 and a normal PT (prothrombin time) and aPTT (activated partial thromboplastin time) explain the bruising.

edits.anchor: when it is high in only about half.
edits.html:
Salient decoyChild abuse: bruises of different colors on an active boy invite it, but bruise color cannot reliably date a bruise. Widespread petechiae, a platelet count of 1,000 and normal clotting times explain the bleeding; a platelet count and coagulation studies belong in most bruising workups for suspected abuse.
Unchecked attributeAbnormal platelet function: von Willebrand disease and Glanzmann thrombasthenia cause bleeding at a normal or near-normal count; this count is 1,000.
Unchecked attributeDecreased platelet production: leukemia and aplastic anemia usually lower more than one cell line; a hemoglobin of 12 and a white count of 6,000 are normal.
True-fact-wrong-slotDisseminated intravascular coagulation: it occurs in an ill patient and prolongs the clotting times, with low fibrinogen and high D-dimer; this boy is well and his clotting times are normal.
